input.question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".
input.ground_truth: It isn't just "goat cheese", it's just that your average American doesn't have enough experiences with goat cheeses to name any particular one. Feta, Kunik, Castelo Branco, and Clochette are all (at least partially) goat cheese that I've eaten personally. I'd think that pretty much everyone in the US has some experience with feta at a minimum.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have two types of milk: one is from cows and the other is from goats.

Cow’s milk is very common, and people have made lots and lots of different cheese types with it over many, many years. They tried making cheese that is soft, hard, smelly, mild, yellow, white, and all sorts of shapes and flavors. That’s why you hear names like cheddar, mozzarella, and brie.

Goat’s milk is less common, and people didn’t make as many different kinds of cheese with it. So, we just call most of the cheese we make from goat’s milk “goat cheese.” It’s like if you have a box of crayons with only a few colors—you don’t have as many names for them as you would if you had every color in the rainbow.

So, cow’s milk cheese has lots of names because there are so many kinds, and goat’s milk cheese is usually just called “goat cheese” because there aren’t as many different types.
